## Purpose

`escalation_resolve` closes an escalation a human has already answered, with the
one sentence that says how it ended. It is the supervisor's half of the Discord
answer loop: a reply in the thread, a tap on one of the post's choice buttons
(spec §5.3), or an answer on the escalation page all land as a verified reply on
the incident, and this command turns that conversation into a terminal state and
an `outcome` the human will read on the collapsed channel post.

It is deliberately *not* a general editor. `expected_revision` is optional — omit
it to resolve the revision the incident has now — and the only text it records is
`outcome`. Sharpening an incident, or withdrawing an unanswered question, is
[`escalation_update`](escalation_update.md); applying a reply through the
question, gate or recovery service it is bound to is
[`escalation_apply_reply`](escalation_apply_reply.md), which writes the terminal
state itself when the guarded action succeeds.

## When a playbook uses it

After the guarded work a human asked for is done and there is nothing left to
ask. The incident's own conversation is the evidence: read it with
`escalation_get`, and resolve only when no entry is still unanswered. It is
refused for an incident nobody has answered yet, which is the honest answer —
"nothing has been decided here" is not an outcome.

Only the owning supervisor may run it. `supervisor_required` excludes trusted
service adapters and non-supervisor principals, so a worker cannot close a
question its human is still reading.

## How it works internally

`EscalationCommandsMixin._cmd_escalation_resolve`
([`src/commands/escalation_commands.py`](../../../src/commands/escalation_commands.py))
validates the outcome, reads the incident through `_escalation_for_caller`, and
walks the legal path to the terminal state with `transition_escalation`. The
stored vocabulary reaches `resolved` only from `resolving`, so an incident that
is one answer ago (`reply_received`) takes two compare-and-set steps and one that
is already `resolving` takes one.

Every step is a compare-and-set against the revision it just read, which is the
fence the rest of the family relies on: a human reply that lands mid-walk
advances the revision, the second step finds nothing to update, and the command
reports `stale_revision` instead of resolving over an answer nobody read. The
final row is announced once as `escalation.updated.v1`.

The Discord post is not edited from here. The escalation delivery tick re-plans
the incident's deliveries from durable state and collapses the one post into its
resolved form, archiving the thread ([`src/escalations/dispatch.py`](../../../src/escalations/dispatch.py)).

## Side effects and persistence

`escalations` gains `state`, `revision`, `updated_at`, `terminal_at`,
`terminal_outcome`, `terminal_evidence` (`{"resolved_by": …, "command":
"escalation_resolve"}`) and `outcome` (`"human"`, which is what keeps the
collapsed post reading *Resolved* rather than *No longer needed*). One
`escalations` event row and one `escalation.updated.v1` event are written. The
reply that made this legal is already durable in `escalation_messages` and is
never modified. Everything survives a restart, and the delivery tick converges
on the collapsed post from the row alone.

## Failure modes and diagnostics

- `invalid_state` — the incident is terminal (terminal states are immutable), or
  nobody has answered it yet; the error names the alternative (`escalation
  update --state cancelled`).
- `stale_revision` — a newer reply arrived; re-read with `escalation_get` and
  resolve again.
- `out_of_scope` — the caller is not the owning supervisor, or the incident
  belongs to another project.
- `spoofed_identity` — the request tried to carry `verified_actor`/`human`/
  `thread_id`; identity is server-derived.
- `not_found` / `invalid_request` — unknown incident, or an `outcome` that is
  empty or longer than 4000 characters.

## Example step

```yaml
- name: close the answered escalation with what was done
  command: escalation_resolve
  args:
    escalation_id: "{{ escalation_id }}"
    outcome: "Shipped from main; the release branch was dropped."
  when: "{{ escalation.state == 'resolving' and escalation.unanswered_entries == 0 }}"
```
